question: with the same features, row counts and fitting procedure, how does training on week-1 recommended (logged) exposures compare with training on week-1 random exposures when the target is week-2 random exposures?

training_sets.random_week1: the adaptation training rows (development users, week 1, main population, scope A; 98,021 rows for the refit)
training_sets.logged_week1: development users' standard exposures of week 1 (streamed from the 27K tar), sampled to match the random set cell by cell on (user, Shanghai date); a cell with fewer logged rows than needed contributes all its rows and the shortfall is recorded and not filled from other cells or users
training_sets.pool_variant: both sets restricted to random-pool videos; the random set is subsampled to the logged pool rows cell by cell with the same rule

features: frozen at the cutoff for every row (as evaluation rows), LR-L2 standardized columns; the M2 form (no iALS input); lambda grid {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1}; selection on report-group week-1 random per-user AUC; refit on all development week-1 rows of each set
comparisons: LR-L2 (6M logged rows, prequential features, days 1-15) vs M2-logged-week1 vs M2-random-week1 on week-2 random exposures
reading: the logged-vs-random difference under identical features, rows and procedure is attributed to the label source (exposure mechanism plus the label distribution it induces); it is a controlled comparison, not a causal identification
